data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's claim that a reliability gain is strictly conditional on the checklist fully specifying the optimal decision function is an unreasonably high threshold. For tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes, a checklist can provide a reliability gain over intuition even if it is imperfect, provided it reduces error rates on average. The counterexample is a checklist that correctly handles 80% of cases where expert intuition errs but fails on 20% of edge cases; the panel using this checklist would still be more reliable on average. SRC_002's edge-case test only distinguishes compliance from gain if the evaluation is powered to detect systematic underperformance, which is not guaranteed within a single evaluation.
